programme: PPARG and PPARD, the two PPAR-family nuclear receptors in this list, drive a lipid-handling transcriptional programme (CD36, FABP4, LPL, OLR1 for lipid uptake; CPT1A, PDK4, ANGPTL4, PPARGC1A, PCK1 for fatty-acid oxidation), with CREBL2 feeding directly into the same switch by targeting both PPARG and CEBPA, the canonical PPARG/CEBPA adipogenic-macrophage differentiation pair.
role_in_a: In lung cancer, this PPARG/PPARD lipid programme operates in tumour cells and tumour-associated macrophages, where fatty-acid oxidation and lipid handling (via FABP4/CD36) modulate macrophage ER stress, ferroptosis sensitivity and metastatic behaviour of the tumour.
role_in_b: In stroke, the same lipid-handling programme operates in plaque and vascular macrophages, where PPARG/PPARD-driven lipid uptake and efferocytosis capacity determine atherosclerotic plaque stability, the usual upstream driver of ischemic stroke.
shared_axis: Both diseases recruit or reprogram myeloid cells in a vascularised tissue, and PPARG/PPARD are the receptors that set the lipid-handling phenotype of those macrophages; the same regulatory switch could plausibly be redeployed in lung tumour-associated macrophages and in plaque macrophages even without any direct causal link between the two diseases.
reasoning: PPARG is independently and directly placed in both lung cancer and a stroke-relevant (atherosclerotic plaque) context by retrieved papers, and its target set is textbook lipid-metabolism/macrophage biology, so the module is real and nameable. But PPARD's disease relevance here rests only on Open Targets percentiles, not on any retrieved paper linking it to either disease, and CREBL2 has no disease association or paper about lung cancer or stroke at all, only about CEBPA/PPARG themselves in an unrelated cancer — so the cross-disease connection is my reasoning about macrophage lipid biology, not something stated in the retrieved record.
support: PMID 41866994 — PPARG-dependent fatty acid oxidation inhibits lung cancer growth; PMID 42294275 — plant-derived EV-like particles suppress lung cancer, retrieved under PPARG; PMID 41317938 — PPARG-FABP4 axis drives macrophage ER stress promoting lung cancer; PMID 40356342 — defective macrophage efferocytosis (a PPARG-linked lipid-clearance process) promotes atherosclerotic plaque instability; PMID 41996726 — a herbal compound acting through PPARG-associated mechanisms improves post-stroke cognitive impairment.
how_to_falsify: Profile macrophages from matched lung tumour tissue and carotid/cerebral atherosclerotic plaque (or a mouse model carrying both a lung tumour and an atherosclerotic lesion), treat with a PPARG/PPARD antagonist (e.g. GW9662 / GSK0660), and test whether the same target genes (CD36, FABP4, LPL, ANGPTL4, CPT1A) move in the same direction in both macrophage populations; divergent or absent responses in one tissue would undercut the claim that a single shared PPAR-driven programme is at work in both.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood|lung, consistent with a myeloid/macrophage-centred story, but only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 84 patient-group comparisons, so the apparent robustness (53/84, 50/84) is not 84 independent replications and should be read cautiously. Several tissue-generic myeloid/vascular regulators (PBX1, EPAS1, IRF8, BCL6, STAT1, ID2/ID3, ETS2, ERG, FOXO1) were removed before ranking, meaning the ordinary blood/lung macrophage or endothelial identity signal has already been stripped out — the PPARG/PPARD signal that remains is not just generic tissue identity. ARNT, which would suggest a hypoxia-driven story, appeared in only one patient group (recurrence 0.19) and did not survive, so no hypoxia/HIF axis should be inferred. The other nine concordant factors (CXXC1, ZKSCAN7, PHF20, ISL1, THAP1, ZNF451, CREB3L1, MNT, GABPA) do not join this lipid-metabolism module by any documented mechanism and are left out of the account rather than forced in.
